findings.claim: Algorithmic directing, scheduling and monitoring can inhibit constructive voice, while algorithmic feedback can support it; system function and role signal matter.
limits: One enterprise and national context; not universal.

findings.claim: The purge-capable loop does not need to classify dissent explicitly: if workers learn that deviation creates scrutiny and voice produces no safe correction route, silence and exit can remove dissonant evidence from the future dataset.
limits: Mechanism hypothesis, not intent or prevalence finding.

findings.claim: Protected concerted activity remains a legal boundary in the United States even though a prior NLRB General Counsel electronic-monitoring memorandum was rescinded.
Validation that uses only compliant survivors cannot determine whether monitoring suppressed high-value criticism, safety reporting, protected activity, or unconventional work methods.
limits: No universal causal rate can be estimated from these sources.

observations.claim: A 2026 matched study of 351 employees and supervisors found that algorithmic directing, scheduling and monitoring inhibited voice through lower felt responsibility for constructive change.
The same study found that algorithmic feedback promoted voice through greater felt responsibility for constructive change.
The decontextualization study distinguishes compliance, alteration and avoidance rather than assuming passive acceptance of surveillance.
limits: Intentions rather than observed long-run outcomes.

observations.claim: Current NLRB guidance states that employers may not discharge, discipline or threaten workers for protected concerted activity, including bringing group complaints or preparing group action.
The NLRB General Counsel rescinded GC 23-02, the prior memorandum on electronic monitoring and algorithmic management, in February 2025.
limits: Rescission does not repeal statutory rights.

observations.claim: OECD survey taxonomy treats conversation content or tone as a monitoring object and sanctioning poor performance as an evaluation use case.
limits: Taxonomy does not prove that protected criticism is scored as poor performance.

title: Voice, dissent, protected activity, and survivor-conditioned learning
